blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — gentamicin therapeutic drug monitoring
stem: A client receiving systemic gentamicin has properly timed peak and trough concentrations measured. According to the current product label, which result exceeds a serum concentration the label says should be avoided?
rationale: Current gentamicin labeling recommends monitoring serum aminoglycoside concentrations when feasible to assure adequate levels and avoid potentially toxic levels. When trough concentrations are monitored, dosage should be adjusted so that levels above 2 mcg/mL are avoided; when peak concentrations are monitored, prolonged levels above 12 mcg/mL should be avoided. Therefore B is the best answer because a trough of 2.6 mcg/mL exceeds the labeled trough concentration to avoid. A and C are below the labeled 12 mcg/mL peak threshold, and D is below the labeled 2 mcg/mL trough threshold. Excessive peak and/or trough concentrations increase renal and eighth-cranial-nerve toxicity risk.
educational_objective: Use gentamicin serum concentration monitoring to avoid potentially toxic exposure; current labeling advises avoiding trough levels above 2 mcg/mL and prolonged peak levels above 12 mcg/mL.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); repackager Cardinal Health 107, LLC; source product distributed by Hospira, Inc.
source_document_title: Gentamicin Sulfate Injection, USP — Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Label revised October 2022; DailyMed updated May 8, 2026; current DailyMed version 14 published May 15, 2026
source_locator: Boxed Warning/WARNINGS: serum aminoglycoside concentrations should be monitored when feasible to assure adequate levels and avoid potentially toxic levels; when monitoring gentamicin peak concentrations, adjust dosage so prolonged levels above 12 mcg/mL are avoided; when monitoring trough concentrations, adjust dosage so levels above 2 mcg/mL are avoided; excessive peak and/or trough concentrations may increase renal and eighth-cranial-nerve toxicity risk.
source_claim_supported: Gentamicin serum concentrations are monitored to avoid potentially toxic exposure; current labeling advises avoiding trough concentrations above 2 mcg/mL and prolonged peak concentrations above 12 mcg/mL because excessive concentrations increase nephrotoxicity and eighth-cranial-nerve toxicity risk.
blueprint_locator: Printed p. 38, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent medication and laboratory data; evaluate client response to medication; assess adverse effects and toxicities; handle and administer high-risk medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt the item as an applied interpretation of properly timed serum concentrations rather than a purpose question with implausible distractors.
Made all four alternatives parallel numeric monitoring results of essentially identical structure and removed the correct-answer length cue.
Used only peak and trough thresholds stated directly in the current product label, with no extrapolated therapeutic range or institution-specific monitoring rule.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B is uniquely above a label-specified concentration to avoid. A and C remain below the labeled prolonged-peak threshold, and D remains below the labeled trough threshold. The stem explicitly states proper timing and asks only about the product-label thresholds, preventing ambiguity from alternate aminoglycoside dosing protocols. No second defensible answer or material cueing remains.
